text: In 1814, a wave of beer flooded London.
say: In eighteen fourteen, a wave of beer flooded London.

text: Over a million pints. In one wave.
say: Over a million pints. In one wave.

text: October 17th. The Horse Shoe Brewery, central London.
say: October seventeenth. The Horse Shoe Brewery, central London.

text: Its giant vat of porter stood 22 feet tall, held together by iron hoops.
say: Its giant vat of porter stood twenty-two feet tall, held together by iron hoops.

text: That afternoon, one hoop slipped off.
say: That afternoon, one hoop slipped off.

text: About an hour later, the whole vat burst.
say: About an hour later, the whole vat burst.

text: The wave knocked open other vats, and smashed down the brewery wall.
say: The wave knocked open other vats, and smashed down the brewery wall.

text: Beer poured into St Giles, one of the poorest slums in London, where families lived in basements.
say: Beer poured into St Giles, one of the poorest slums in London, where families lived in basements.

text: The inquest called it an act of God.
say: The inquest called it an act of God.

text: And the brewery? Parliament gave it back the tax it had paid on the beer.
